findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never visited, posted in, or otherwise interacted with the topic (for example, opening the unsubscribe URL directly or after the row was removed). The next line calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. The action should create/update the record through the existing TopicUser.change mechanism (as set_notifications does) so a missing row is created with the muted/regular level.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by a plain GET request
findings.body: The new server route is GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and this action immediately mutates notification_level and saves it. Email security scanners, link prefetchers, browser pre-rendering, or a third party tricking a logged-in user into loading the URL (CSRF via GET, which Rails forgery protection does not cover) will unsubscribe/mute the user without any intentional click or confirmation. The GET should only render a confirmation page and the mutation should require a non-GET request, as the Ember notification dropdown already can perform.

findings.title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses notification-change bookkeeping and leaves stale state
findings.body: Mutating tu.notification_level and calling tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the established path used by set_notifications: it stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, runs observe_after_save_callbacks_for, and publishes a MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change event. Because @topic_view was also built before the mutation, the rendered/serialized response and any already-open client can keep showing the old watching/tracking level even though the database changed, and downstream observers never learn of the change. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

findings.title: topicUnsubscribe route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear
findings.body: The topic resource defined just above already has a child route fromParamsNear with path '/:nearPost', i.e. /t/:slug/:id/:nearPost, which matches the literal segment 'unsubscribe'. Ember's router recognises routes in definition order, so /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe is matched as the normal topic page with nearPost='unsubscribe' before the later top-level topicUnsubscribe route is considered; the unsubscribe template/controller therefore never renders on a full page load or transition. The unsubscribe route needs to be defined so it wins recognition over the :nearPost wildcard (or handled inside the topic route).

findings.title: Emails with add_unsubscribe_link but no topic unsubscribe_url now raise
findings.body: The server locale string unsubscribe_link now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, and both body (line 90) and html_part (line 67) call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. MessageBuilder is generic: any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without also passing unsubscribe_url (previously valid, and the behaviour the existing specs exercised before they were edited to pass a URL) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to deliver the email instead of falling back to the plain user-preferences unsubscribe text. The per-topic sentence should only be appended when unsubscribe_url is present.

findings.title: No test covers the new unsubscribe behaviour end-to-end
findings.body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into an existing builder fixture but adds no assertion that the topic unsubscribe URL appears in the text body or HTML part, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (level transitions watching/tracking->regular and regular->muted, missing TopicUser row, wrong slug redirect, JSON vs HTML). The core state-transition logic of this feature can regress or crash without any test failing.
